target_customer: Originally US senders of remittances to Latin America; now banks, fintechs and wallet providers that embed instant cross border P2P payments
problem: Sending money from the US to other countries is slow, cash based and inconvenient for senders and receivers.
business_model: B2B2C payments infrastructure: API, embeddable payment blocks and white label checkout for financial institutions, earning on transfers (fee model not stated in sources)

founders.name: Enrique Perezalonso
prior_employers: McKinsey & Co. and other consulting firms
founders.background_notes: YC page: 25+ years across traditional financial institutions and fintechs in marketing, product, operations and sales.

founders.name: Andrew Mason
previous_startups: FlashGrade (backed by Intel Capital, per YC page)

founders.name: Gregory Piccolo
founders.background_notes: Listed as Co-founder & CTO on the Cowboy Ventures portfolio page; the page gives no bio and he is not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Remitly
competitors.what: Digital remittance app; Mexico corridor launched 2015
competitors.traction_then: IPO filing said India, the Philippines and Mexico were about 75% of 2020 revenue and send volume
competitors.funding_then: Listed on Nasdaq 2021-09-23 at about $7B valuation (about 2 months after the batch)

competitors.name: Wise
competitors.what: Digital money transfer benchmark on price and product
competitors.funding_then: Listed in London in 2021-07 at about $11B valuation per FXC Intelligence

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs payout partnerships and compliance in many corridors plus real time rails integration; mostly standard engineering with hard licensing and partner work.

defensibility.rationale: A network of 50+ corridors and bank integrations (company claim) is slow to copy, but remittance is a crowded field with large rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents scaled digital offerings but no source shows one copying Palla's bank embedded model; Palla pivoted toward B2B infrastructure.

market_need_then: The YC page cites a $65B a year US to abroad P2P market; later coverage cites over $155B sent from the US to Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023. Remittance was cash heavy and slow in 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses palla.com (YC site field); acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Clean fintech infrastructure site; partners can apply their own brand
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and bank focused: the platform for instant cross-border P2P payments

brand_strength.rationale: A white label B2B product where partner brands face the user; coverage is about funding, not the brand.

pivots.from: Consumer style P2P remittance app for US senders
pivots.to: Infrastructure layer sold to banks and fintechs
pivots.why: Palla's CEO told Refresh Miami the company was built as an infrastructure layer rather than a consumer app; the exact date of the shift is not stated

outcome_analysis: Palla stayed active and raised a $14.5M Series A led by Revolution Ventures in 2025-05, almost four years after the batch, with about $15M raised in total per a spokesperson. It moved from consumer P2P remittance toward selling payment rails to banks across Latin America, which sidestepped consumer rivals like Remitly and Wise. Founders had banking and fintech experience. Growth looks steady but slow for the YC cohort.
notes: Series A of $14.5M in 2025-05 is stated by Axios, fintech.global, Payments Dive and Crowdfund Insider (the Business Wire release returned HTTP 403 and was not opened). Seed: Extruct lists $125,000 on 2021-08-22 with Y Combinator and CB Insights shows an undisclosed 2021 note; unverified so not recorded. Total raised: spokesperson says about $15M, CB Insights says $17.45M. Competitor sources are dated in 2021-07 to 2021-09, during or just after the S21 batch. The pivot date is not stated. Founders: the YC page names two; the Cowboy Ventures portfolio page lists a third co-founder, Gregory Piccolo (CTO), added without further background.
